messages:
derek: quick sync — proposal for harmonizing trace/metric/log headers so we can do SLO-aware sampling and stable cost attribution across ingest tiers. sketch below, want feedback before i put up an RFC.
maria: SGTM. high level — are we aiming for one canonical key for tenant+feature, or multiple keys with a mapping layer?
shweta: mapping layer feels safer short term. one canonical key requires sweeping SDK changes. but mapping layer increases runtime join complexity.
alex: agree with shweta. mapping layer + gradual SDK rollouts. we should version the header though (v1, v2) so routing logic is explicit.
derek: yep. proposal: add a small stable header x-rd-telemetry with compact k=v pairs; we keep x-rd-telemetry-v for schema version. example:
```http
x-rd-telemetry: t=acct:ACCT123;f=feature:chat;cohort=gold
x-rd-telemetry-v: 1
```
maria: that compact form is nice. does "cohort" imply sampling policy? or is it just a hint to upstream?
shweta: cohort -> sampling_hint. runtime might treat it as hard (must) for billing cohorts, soft for performance queues. we need clear semantics.
derek: propose semantics: cohort is authoritative for cost-buckets (billing/chargeback). sampling_hint is best-effort for latency SLO routing. add explicit fields: s=hint:low_latency or s=sample:1/100
alex: minor nit: parsing k=v pairs inline is cheap, but please document escaping and max header size. also watch proxies trimming long headers.
ops-bot: deploybot: canary deploy added for runtime-router:v2 at 10% in us-west on 2026-04-01 03:00 UTC
maria: good point about proxies. maybe also duplicate minimal keys into a single short token: x-rd-mini: <base64(t|f|cohort)> for perf-sensitive paths.
shweta: love that. mini token for edge, full for internal. runtime can prefer mini if present.
derek: tradeoffs: mapping layer means ingest needs an enrichment step to resolve feature->product mapping and expand tenant metadata. that adds CPU but keeps SDK churn low.
alex: can we push enrichment to a lightweight sidecar so host processes don't pay spike? sidecar can batch lookups and cache results.
maria: sidecar seems reasonable. ops concerns: memory/cpu on low-tier hosts. we should define backpressure fallback: if enrichment fails, tag as cohort=unknown and route to default cheap path.
derek: yes — fallback policy in proposal: cohort=unknown => route to best-effort queue with cached model (lower cost). also emit a span annotation: enrichment.miss=true.
shweta: we also need to think about rekeying existing traces for historical cost attribution. if we change field names, queries should still resolve old keys.
alex: add an alias table in the analytics layer for old-key -> new-key mapping. small ETL job to backfill recent windows where possible.
derek: final open Qs: 1) header names/limits, 2) versioning strategy, 3) enrichment placement (sidecar vs central), 4) sampling contract semantics. i'll turn this into RFC draft tomorrow.
maria: i can take point on header docs and proxy compatibility tests.
shweta: i'll prototype sidecar enrichment and bench lookup latency.
alex: i'll scope the analytics aliasing/backfill steps.
ops-bot: reminder: RFC templates are in /docs/rfcs — tag it obsv-schema so it routes to eng-platform reviewers.
derek: thanks — will post RFC 4623460000-obsv-header-unify-rfc.json tomorrow and ping reviewers. :thumbsup:
